RC10 improves the path from a user prompt to the evidence the coding model reads. It keeps one
fixed coding model by default. JEV remains optional, and existing sharing declarations still decide
which metadata and source bodies may leave the machine.

- Prompt packets name their execution worktree and native entry. `context-route --entry <id>`
  revalidates and reuses that packet without another selection. A bare context command cannot
  identify the current host turn; use an explicit entry or refresh with the current request.
- One compact request layout sends shared instructions once and preserves each permitted item's
  meaning. Receipts distinguish cached descriptors, approved descriptors and facts actually sent.
  The existing configured source window now fills from the assessed metadata order throughout.
- Answered uncertain scores help decide which file or passage to inspect next. They stay visibly
  uncertain and cannot grant authority, establish correctness or enlarge an excerpt allowance.
- Projects can declare existing Markdown runbooks in `context_router.procedure_sources`. Their
  sections enter the existing passage pipeline alongside implementation and test evidence.
  Required guidance and explicit pins stay first; quoted procedures do not execute themselves.
- Packet fitting preserves ordinary bounded excerpts and gives larger procedures and confirmed
  extensions turns within the same envelope. Small files retain their helpers and fixtures. Original
  ranges, incomplete units and omissions remain visible. Native hooks honor
  the declared route envelope without a second optional 8 KiB ceiling.
- The native profile can set `context_router.optional_excerpt_bytes`, using the same allowance as
  the manual command. Defaults stay unchanged. Existing literal imports can keep a confirmed test
  beside its captured, non-negative implementation without pinning it or changing uncertainty.
- The maintained index retains more bounded descriptors and preserves function-declaration prose, Kotlin
  enum/quoted names and test annotations. Native measured usage settles conservative rate estimates; unknown usage keeps its
  reservation. One 30-second operation limit, shared spending and admission ceilings remain.
- Passive telemetry reads filter recent matching work before applying limits. Retention, incomplete
  ingestion and unknown native reads, usage and accepted outcomes remain explicit.

Local proof covers isolated installed hooks with fixture inference, exact reuse, fallback, worktree
identity and source permissions. Frozen-source library simulations use an explicitly declared
64-file, 8 KiB ordinary excerpt and 48,000-byte optional packet profile; smaller profiles retain
misses and do not have the same retrieval qualification. Simulations retain failures and corrections; repeated cases
are regression proof, not new independent holdouts. These checks do not establish accepted-task
token savings, device behavior or native host adoption in another checkout.

Adopt at a pause seam in each execution worktree. Review descriptor/body permissions and the packet
envelope, opt in to passage questions and a small set of runbooks, and keep the coding model fixed.
The procedure declaration is optional; installing RC10 does not enable JEV or upgrade sibling pins.
